children: Shares of Valvoline rose after the company posted higher revenue in its most recent quarter, boosted by an increase in same-store sales.
Shares rose 13% to $37.81 on Thursday. The stock is up 28% year to date.

The maker of motor oils' fourth-quarter revenue rose 22% to $554.1 million, helped by a 9.4% increase in same-store sales. Analysts polled by FactSet expected $568.6 million in revenue on 9% same-store sales growth.
Valvoline posted a fourth-quarter profit of $9.4 million, or 8 cents a share, compared with $25 million, or 20 cents a share, the year earlier.
On an adjusted basis, earnings per share were 42 cents, in line with analyst expectations, according to FactSet.

Chief Executive Lori Flees said the company has executed well through a changing supply environment. For full-year 2027, the company guided for same-store sales between 5% to 7% on revenue between $2.25 billion to $2.35 billion. Analysts expect same-store sales growth at 5.6% on $2.32 revenue.
Valvoline expects 2027 adjusted earnings per share between $1.85 and $2.05, while analysts expect $1.95 a share.
